title: SharePoint admin center: Data access governance report of sites a group can access
summary: Hold: the promise to show every site a group can access omits Microsoft's explicit exclusion of access inherited through nested groups. The cost rationale also says only administrator time is involved despite documenting paid entitlement requirements. The roadmap dates, licensing options and published PowerShell calls otherwise check out.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The group report lists every site a given group can access, without qualifying the group types or nested-group access.
claims.quote: Group reports don't expand nested-group permissions. If a security group is a member of another group, access granted to the parent group isn't included in the nested group's report.
claims.fix: Replace the summary's first sentence with 'SharePoint administrators will get a report of site access for Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Entra security groups, excluding access inherited through nested groups.' Add to the Learn description in What's changing: 'SharePoint groups and distribution lists are not supported inputs, and group reports exclude access inherited through nested-group membership.' These qualifications are stated at https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/data-access-governance-site-permissions-users-report. Qualify the other unqualified descriptions of the report's reach the same way.

claims.claim: The group report is reached through SharePoint admin center > Reports > Data access governance > Site permissions for users or groups > View reports > Create report > Create report for > Groups.
claims.quote: From the Data access governance landing page, select View reports under Site permissions for users or groups. ... Select Create report ... Under Create report for, select Users or Groups, then select Next.
claims.fix: The printed labels are in the documented order, and the navigation prefix is documented at the cited overview. To finish the route to running a report, use 'Reports > Data access governance > Site permissions for users or groups > View reports > Create report > Create report for > Groups > Create and run'. In the row note add 'Before Create and run, choose the groups, specify Scope and provide Report name.' The intermediate selections and final button are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/data-access-governance-site-permissions-users-report.

claims.claim: The PowerShell guide documents Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionsReport -ReportType Snapshot -Workload SharePoint -Name <name> -TargetGroups <groups> for group reports.
claims.quote:
Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight `
    -ReportEntity PermissionsReport `
    -ReportType Snapshot `
    -Workload SharePoint `
    -Name "GroupPermissionsReport" `
    -TargetGroups $groups

claims.claim: TargetGroups takes the group objects returned by Get-MgGroup.
claims.quote: Retrieve the groups with Get-MgGroup, then pass the returned group objects directly to the TargetGroups parameter.
